tasks.short: Prepare patient progress reports and charts

steps.what: Review patient reactions and capture progress observations, measures and limitations
Prepare reports and charts from checked progress entries
Check reports for clinical meaning and submit them to the treatment team

tasks.design: Configure the patient record system {OTHER} to populate report sections and charts from therapist-checked entries. The therapist retains interpretation of progress or regression and checks the exact report before sending it to the treatment team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports can require repeating observations already captured in the patient record.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report templates can reuse explicit entries without inventing clinical conclusions.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting reactions and whether measures indicate meaningful change.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding the patient's experience and contextualising apparent progress.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeat copying while retaining responsibility for the clinical account.

reach.learn: Team reporting requirements and measure definitions

evidence.claim: Structured entries can populate fixed reports and charts; task-specific savings and clinical interpretation remain unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers reviewing available session observations, capturing report entries and submitting the progress report; delivering therapy and original clinical assessment are separate and unchanged.

Therapist produces patient ID, session date, goal ID, observed reaction, measure, unit and explanatory limitations in s1; capture and source checking are counted. Missing or inconsistent entries require manual report preparation, never an inferred progress flag.
The {OTHER} slot is the patient record system. Test native reports and chart configuration before custom code; already populated reports earn no new saving.
No extra patient or treatment-team recording is required; their existing observation and treatment work remains unchanged.
unknowns: Available structured measures and report templates
research_questions: Does configured report assembly save time after source capture and therapist validation are included?

incremental.description: Patient record configuration and access upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Patient, source entry versions, reporting period, report text and charts; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70, gross30 minus focal upkeep8 gives net22. Range allows existing report population and narrative exceptions to absorb most or all benefit; clinical meaning checks remain fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Develop discharge plans by assessing needs, discussing support and agreeing appropriate recreational follow-up

tasks.design: Retain individual discharge planning and record the agreed plan in the patient record system {OTHER}. Existing templates in {DOCS} can guide completeness, but they do not establish that the person has suitable support or access to activities.
tasks.previous_blocker: A safe plan depends on individual needs, preferences and actual support.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing documentation can support discussion without a new decision system.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether suggested activities are appropriate and feasible after discharge.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing a practical plan with the patient and treatment team.
tasks.altitude: Discharge planning responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate recreational follow-up with the wider discharge plan
reach.learn: Community support access and clinical handoff procedures

evidence.claim: Individual discharge planning requires clinical and interpersonal judgement; no task-specific labour saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary covers the therapist's contribution to discharge planning; other clinicians' decisions, service provision and patient activity remain outside it.
Therapist verifies needs, preferences, support and access during s1; no free structured readiness or available-service flag is assumed.
The {OTHER} slot is the patient record system. Test existing templates before custom code; no new automation is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the existing planning method remains unchanged.
research_questions: Does observed planning contain separable repeated copying after clinical discussion and support verification?

already_counted.description: Needs review, support verification and planning discussion

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Individual planning, support verification and discussion retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retains therapeutic decisions while reducing repeated report assembly where present.
reach: Prepare clear progress summaries and coordinated follow-up plans
role.ambitious_version: Use verified documentation gains to spend more time understanding patient needs and feasible follow-up.
